findings: THE TARGET PLATES WERE ALREADY ON DISK. Thorn's n=0 is an ANCHOR-CHOICE failure, not an acquisition failure. board.json anchors thorn on REF-A3 (Telvanni grown mushroom towers) and ALL FIVE REF-A3 plates are square crops — 0 of 5 composition-valid — so the row can never be set whatever the town looks like. REF-A19 ('Waterside settlement at Hla Oad: a moored longboat with a green-and-white striped sail beside stilted shacks') has 6 composition-valid plates; REF-A11 (Bitter Coast swamp — boardwalks, standing water, mist) has 3. Both clear the board's own >=3 threshold. No acquisition was needed and none was done.
RI-VIS09's composition-valid rule was used as written and not loosened: framing == 'full frame, native aspect, uncropped' AND sky_visible == true.

THORN'S ARCHITECTURE IS DESCRIBED THREE DIFFERENT WAYS AND ONLY ONE RENDERS. thorn.json architecture_kit says black-thorn thatch over a rotted great hall, every structure a lean-to; thorn.json architecture_grammar.primary and all 18 buildings[].grammar say `salt-block` (which architecture.json assigns to the stone-wastes, not to thornmarsh); world-art.js:30 says `spiral-palisade`, which is not one of architecture.json's nine grammars at all. The renderer uses none of them: lib/kits.js keys GRAMMARS by SETTLEMENT id and gives thorn roofs ['roof.reed','roof.hip'].

RULING E1 MEASUREMENT (silhouettes, not parts), via the renderer's own planSettlement -> assignVariantSalts -> previewSilhouette: thorn 2 distinct roof profiles over 18 buildings (reed x13, hip x5). Lilmoth 3 (the best in the game); archon/helstrom/soulrest 2; blackrose/gideon/stormhold 1. NO SETTLEMENT REACHES 5, and >=5 is UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: GRAMMARS defines only three roof ids in total (roof.reed, roof.hip, roof.shell).

INSTRUMENT CONTROL for the above: a first run passed a constant seed and reported 1 roof profile for ALL EIGHT towns, because roofChoice returns gram.roofs[0] for a fixed seed — an artefact of my seeding, not a fact about the game. Feeding the real per-building salts moves six of the eight and leaves three at 1, so the constant-seed arm is a working negative control that collapses every town to one profile while the live arm does not. Roofline heights are seed-independent and identical in both arms.

THE FIRST EXTERIOR IN THE GAME IS A QUAY WITH NO TIDELINE. `tideline` is a real grammar property in lib/kits.js and ONLY `lilmoth` sets it (tideline: 1.45, drownedRole: 'stone'); the drowned-storey path at exterior.js:1613 already works against it. exterior.js:1608's comment says 'it is deliberately the starting town's' — written when Lilmoth was believed to be the starting town. GRAMMARS.thorn has no tideline and support:'post' rather than 'pier'.

tidewrack-quay holds exactly TWO buildings (barge-hold, writ-house) and NO props at all. Both reuse other meshes: barge-hold -> tavern-1-barge-hold, writ-house -> shop-2-writ-house. Six ready quay parts exist next door and are pure reuse: lil_pile_cluster, lil_stilt_platform, lil_tide_mark, lil_boom_chain, lil_customs_hall, sou_silt_quay.

THORN'S FOUR BESPOKE EXTERIOR KIT PARTS ARE ALL PROPS, NOT BUILDINGS: tho_needle_stack (a woodpile), tho_charter_post (a signpost), tho_bow_rack, tho_sapwell_kerb. Lilmoth has six including lil_customs_hall (a whole building) and a full quay vocabulary. EXT_KIT holds 37 parts total. NOTE: the first four ids in every town's architecture_kit.meshes are interior prop meshes reused outdoors — that is by design (exterior.js's own comment), not a defect, and it is the same in all eight towns.

VERTICALITY IS ALREADY IN THE DATA AND NOTHING MAKES IT READ. The quay doors sit at y=0 and the town centre at y=13.31 m about 50 m away — a ~15% climb on the player's first walk. Roofline heights span 3.4-9.0 m.

'A thicket you walk into and cannot see out of' is the town's own identity line; thornmarsh's terrain already declares depth:'hook-arch-thickets' (world-art.js:17) and nothing closes the sky over Thorn's streets. Not yet built.

MATERIAL RESPONSE HAS n=0 AND HONESTLY SO. pixel_metrics_valid is false on all 89 Morrowind plates (RI-VIS09 §3.3), so no plate may ever be a material-response target; and my frames are software. That axis is recorded unset rather than guessed.
stormhold is in the same n=0 position as thorn and is not this piece's job; whoever fixes thorn's anchor should look at it in the same pass.

OBSERVED FROM THE RUNNING GAME, UNRESOLVED: the harness reports the Tidewrack quay spawn [3808.6, 0, 909.36] as region 'western-rootlands', while thorn.json declares Thorn's region as 'thornmarsh'. Region drives terrain, flora and palette in world-art.js, so if that is the world's real answer rather than a harness artefact the quay is being dressed as Lilmoth's region. Worth ten minutes BEFORE chunk 2 changes any material.

THE BARGE HOLD — the first room of the game — ALREADY READS WELL: timber planking and beams, a warm lamp down a ladder, crates with weight. It is not the weak part; the exterior is. Two unfinished elements seen and named rather than fixed: a flat untextured orange hexagon floating at head height in the barge hold, and a plain white rectangle floating in front of the shelf wall in the writ house. Ordinary mid-build state, recorded so the next person sees them.
